play_name: See if a friendship goes both ways
behavioral_target: Always being the one who reaches out first in a friendship.
trigger: You want to talk to a friend or make plans with them.
old_play: You reach out first, every time.
function_of_old_play: Reaching out first keeps the friendship going from your side.
new_play: Reach out when you want to. Then leave some space and see if they reach back before you reach again.
what_to_expect: It might feel quiet for a while. You may learn a friend reaches back, or that they do not.
why_supports_task: Seeing who reaches back helps you tell which friendships are shared and which are one-sided. This friendship work does not sit in one relationship phase.
context_limitations: Reaching out first is fine sometimes. This is about when it is always you. A friend may also be going through a hard time.
review_reason: Cross-Phase source gap: no competency maps and there is no single developmental task. The maintaining role is inferred from the one-sided-friendship context.
